title: Standardise names, titles, emails and phones
prompt:
The same job title appears as `Software Engineer`, `software  engineer` and `SOFTWARE ENGINEER`, so a count by title gives three answers. Emails and phone numbers are just as mixed.

Write `employee_clean(employees)`. It starts from your `employee_view(employees)` and rewrites the text fields below into one standard form each. Every other column, and every row, stays as it is.
rules: `job_title`: no spaces at either end, one space between words, each word starting with a capital and the rest lower case, except `of`, which stays lower case (`Head of Data`).
`email`: no spaces at either end, all lower case.
`phone`: the last ten digits written as `555-201-3344`, whatever the format was. A missing phone stays missing.
`department_id`: no spaces at either end, upper case (`D02`).
Return `employee_view`'s columns in the same order, one row per input row.
hints: Call `employee_view(employees)` and `select` from it, replacing the four columns with cleaned versions and keeping their names with `.alias`.
For the title: `F.trim`, then `F.regexp_replace(..., r"\s+", " ")`, then `F.initcap`. `initcap` gives `Head Of Data`, so one more `regexp_replace` turns `" Of "` back into `" of "`.

For the phone: keep the digits with `regexp_replace("phone", "[^0-9]", "")`, keep the last ten with `F.substring(digits, -10, 10)`, then rebuild the dashes with groups: `r"^(\d{3})(\d{3})(\d{4})$"` and `"$1-$2-$3"`.
explanation: Each field gets one rule, written once as a column expression. Trimming and collapsing runs of spaces before `initcap` means `  software  engineer ` and `SOFTWARE ENGINEER` both become `Software Engineer`; the final `regexp_replace` puts the small word `of` back in lower case. Phone numbers are rebuilt from their digits, so the format they arrived in doesn't matter, and keeping the last ten drops the `+1` country code. String functions return `NULL` for `NULL`, so a missing phone needs no special case. Because `employee_clean` starts from `employee_view`, the columns and their order are already right.
